newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen strengthening in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen strengthening in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to continue to strengthen for the rest of the season to June 30, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said.
"Confidence in the wool market is noticeably strong, evidenced by the dramatic price rises last week," Wesfarmers said in its weekly market preview.
Last week, the eastern market indicator jumped 25 cents to a 21-month high of 700 cents a kg clean while the western market indicator rose 29 cents to 658 cents a kg clean.
About 52,100 bales are on offer this week in Sydney and Fremantle, significantly below last week's, it said.

Wesfarmers said the market strength was due to several factors. These included: Sufficient demand to continue generating orders with an increase in Chinese activity, the fall of the Australian dollar in recent weeks and, with wool supply being limited over coming weeks, this week's small offering is encouraging competition.

These factors are expected to continue in the short term, and therefore, the wool market outlook is for further price increases this week and a general positive trend over the rest of the season, Wesfarmers said.
